video_title: Explaining Steph Curry, Ayesha Curry's Charity Impact In Oakland

quotes.speaker: Christopher Helfrich
quotes.summary_phrase: Eat. Learn. Play. foundation's growth and impact in Oakland
quotes.excerpt: the generosity that Workday has brought to this event and that's allowed it to grow

text_blocks.speaker: Dalton Johnson
text_blocks.text: Here is the seventh annual Workday Charity Classic event benefiting Eat. Learn. Play. Starting with you, Chris, when I say the number seven, how exciting does that feel to get to, we are closing in on a decade doing this, of course with Aneel as well too?

text_blocks.speaker: Christopher Helfrich
text_blocks.text: Time flies. It is pretty surreal that we are at seven years and to see the way that this event is growing, it is pretty remarkable. The generosity that Workday has brought to this event and that's allowed it to grow into something that's raised well over $10 million now that's 100% of that goes right back out in the community. It is remarkable, it is gratifying, and it is also the most fun day of the year.

quotes.speaker: Aneel Bhusri
quotes.summary_phrase: Aneel Bhusri on the Curry family's community impact
quotes.excerpt: it all starts with this guy and the Currys. We are just the enabler

text_blocks.speaker: Dalton Johnson
text_blocks.text: Aneel, do you allow yourself to look back at the beginning of this and see how much it has grown to these stages?

text_blocks.speaker: Aneel Bhusri
text_blocks.text: I haven't recently until I drove up here today and I thought, my god, the seventh year. It all starts with this guy and the Currys. We are just the enabler. We bring together a bunch of people that are willing to invest in what Steph and Ayesha and Chris want to do in Oakland and the Bay Area for kids. It is pretty amazing what they have done. I would say this is a great event, but what they are doing in the community is just mind-boggling.

quotes.speaker: Christopher Helfrich
quotes.summary_phrase: Eat. Learn. Play. impact on Oakland school playgrounds
quotes.excerpt: over 10,000 kids every day are going and playing, learning and growing on these state of the art spaces

text_blocks.speaker: Dalton Johnson
text_blocks.text: Just 10 days ago was the 25th school year that Eat. Learn. Play. has transformed in Oakland. When I say 25, what does that number mean to you?

text_blocks.speaker: Christopher Helfrich
text_blocks.text: It means that there are a lot of kids who are finally getting the spaces that they deserve. When we started remodeling schoolyards, across the entire district there is 49 elementary schools. Really the play spaces is just blacktop and an old playground and a couple basketball hoops. But now, through this work, over 10,000 kids every day are going and playing, learning and growing on these state of the art spaces. That ambition was really driven by Workday and Aneel. When we did our second, it was Aneel who called me the next day and said that was amazing, can we do all of them? And that's been the journey that we have been on over the last couple of years. We are over halfway there and we are not going to stop until every kid in Oakland has the best spaces possible where they can play every day.

quotes.speaker: Christopher Helfrich
quotes.summary_phrase: Steph and Ayesha Curry's ambition and community commitment
quotes.excerpt: how can we disrupt things in a really positive way all in the interest of making sure kids

text_blocks.speaker: Dalton Johnson
text_blocks.text: Christopher, you keep using the word ambition. I love to hear that word, especially for an event like this for both of you. How have you seen the Currys show their ambition throughout the Bay Area and Oakland, and of course specifically?

text_blocks.speaker: Christopher Helfrich
text_blocks.text: You see the way that Steph, you see Steph on the basketball court and you see some of the stuff that he tries that no one else will or has. I like to think we have a little bit of that at Eat. Learn. Play. where we see a situation that might need some fixing and we are just ambitious enough to go, you know what, that doesn't have to be the status quo. How can we disrupt things in a really positive way all in the interest of making sure kids in Oakland have the happy, healthy, joyful childhoods that they deserve.

quotes.speaker: Aneel Bhusri
quotes.summary_phrase: Aneel Bhusri on Steph and Ayesha Curry's character
quotes.excerpt: he is one of the greatest basketball players of all time. He is an even better human being

text_blocks.speaker: Aneel Bhusri
text_blocks.text: Steph and Ayesha, they just always show up. They just show up and that goes so far and so long in the community. I have known Steph for a long time. He is one of the greatest basketball players of all time. He is an even better human being and the same applies to Ayesha and that is what is so magical about it.

quotes.speaker: Christopher Helfrich
quotes.summary_phrase: Steph Curry winning the Muhammad Ali Sports Humanitarian Award
quotes.excerpt: Steph winning the Muhammad Ali Humanitarian Award, all for the work that he and Ayesha do in Oakland

text_blocks.speaker: Dalton Johnson
text_blocks.text: That is my final question right there as I think about the award that he won this year when it comes to the Muhammad Ali Sports Humanitarian Award. That was an award that it felt like he wanted to share part of with both of you and with all of Oakland, with the entire Bay Area. How awesome was it to see him on that stage winning an award that was bigger than basketball?

text_blocks.speaker: Christopher Helfrich
text_blocks.text: That was a special moment, Steph winning the Muhammad Ali Humanitarian Award, all for the work that he and Ayesha do in Oakland to be there with Aneel and get to watch it. It was great and the Currys are the best and it was really nice to see them be recognized and honored for the work that they do literally day in and day out to help Oakland kids.
